title: Seal Rocks: Perspective Warp, Sky Widening, and Directional Light in Coastal Photoshop

locations.name: Seal Rocks (probable)
locations.basis: filename 'Seal Rocks.mp4' and folder name imply location; transcript references coastal rocks/sea stacks but not explicit location

summary: The video presents a coastal Photoshop workflow centered on salvaging a shot of sea stacks by blending, warping, and light-control techniques. The speaker explains starting with two images to copy a perfect wave onto another frame when shooting on a tripod, then addresses composition fixes when people intrude and a perfect wave isn’t available. A series of corrective tools follows: a perspective warp to align rocks and remove distractions, clone-stamping with heavy sampling to clone out foreground elements, and a horizon-straightening operation. The narrative then shifts to creating directional light via blur plus luminosity and staged color grading to simulate light coming from one side, followed by tonal-based color adjustments to unify water color. Other core steps include selective color adjustments (50-150 style), auto HDR for texture, and background replacement from alternative frames to fix lens/surface issues. The tutorial also covers sky widening through RAW distortion/scale, the rule of trapezoids for wide-angle widening, cloud-streak creation, and careful edge blending to maintain believable depth. The overall aim is a sunset-like, three-dimensional feel with strong directional light and cohesive color throughout the scene.

sections.title: Wave blending and the need for a perfect frame
sections.description: Introduces the coastal shot and explains how to blend a better wave from a neighboring frame when timing or composition is imperfect.

sections.title: Dealing with people in the frame
sections.description: Explains the problem of people in the shot and the strategy of finding another capture or planning field changes to make later blending possible.

sections.title: Perspective warp and initial clone blending
sections.description: Uses a warped duplicate of the rock to align geometry, then clones and hard-blends the people out of the frame.

sections.title: Refining the clone-out with multi-sampling
sections.description: Continues reshaping and cloning the scene, emphasizing that hard edges and many sample points are needed to hide the removal convincingly.

sections.title: Correcting the horizon after the warp
sections.description: Straightens the tilted horizon introduced by the earlier warping and notes the tradeoff between removing distractions and preserving the original rock shape.

sections.title: Making the scene feel directional
sections.description: Argues that lens distortion and the earlier edits can be accepted creatively, then shifts to the goal of building strong light coming from the right side.

sections.title: Blur plus luminosity and basic color shaping
sections.description: Builds a distant, hazier feel with blur and luminosity, then pushes warmth and blue-green water color to simulate sunset lighting.

sections.title: Tonal-based color adjustment for consistency
sections.description: Uses tonal color rebuilding to unify inconsistent water and sky color, while noting existing banding and restoring the original rock detail.

sections.title: Restoring detail and expanding dynamic range
sections.description: Brings back detail in the middle ground and reworks color and contrast after earlier shortcuts caused uneven results.

sections.title: Selective Color and texture in the splash
sections.description: Applies the selective-color recipe to boost light on the rocks, then uses darker counter-adjustments and HDR-style texture to emphasize the splash.

sections.title: Haze, banding, and the search for a cleaner background
sections.description: Tames the overly crisp areas, diagnoses persistent banding, and looks for a cleaner alternative frame to replace the contaminated background.

sections.title: Replacing the background and matching reflections
sections.description: Grades the alternate frame to a warm sunset look, aligns the sun and reflections, and blends the new background into the foreground water.

sections.title: Cleaning salt spots and finishing the base composite
sections.description: Uses healing on the water spots, preserving texture while clearing the lens contamination before moving on to creative widening.

sections.title: Widening the scene with RAW distort/scale and cloud streaks
sections.description: Demonstrates two widening methods: RAW distortion/scale for the sky and the rule of trapezoids for making the composition feel broader.

sections.title: Directional glow and blur-plus-luminosity depth
sections.description: Builds glowing light through the rocks and across the background, using blur plus luminosity to create stronger depth and atmospheric separation.

sections.title: Final water-light pass and wrap-up
sections.description: Applies the same light treatment to the water, then reviews the before-and-after effect and ends the demonstration.
